consensus: There is no published primer for the deck the pilot is describing: every fetchable drain-engine Edgar list (Itzlsp's 'Life Drain', Gregory's Midrange Markov, Furtado's Draftsim guide) runs the Exquisite Blood + Sanguine Bond / Vito loop as its backup win, and the cEDH decklist database holds no Edgar at all. What the drain-tagged data agrees on, once the loop is subtracted, is a three-layer shape. Layer one is per-death drain, and this deck already runs its two most-run per-death pieces (Blood Artist 429/484 and Cruel Celebrant 334/484 in the 484-deck Lifedrain theme). Layer two is big evasive Vampires whose body carries the drain: Malakir Bloodwitch (261/484, 53.9%) and Twilight Prophet (245/484, 50.6%) are the two drain-carrying Vampires this deck lacks that clear half of Lifedrain lists (Edgar, Charmed Groom 264 and Clavileño 258 also clear half but carry no drain; Exquisite Blood 328 is excluded by the pilot); Vein Ripper (109/484, 22.5%) and Falkenrath Noble (103/484, 21.3%) are the next tier. Layer three is the one-sided sweeper, and Olivia's Wrath (273/484, 56.4%) is the most-run sweeper in all three drain-adjacent themes, and in the Aristocrats theme more lists run it (808/1500) than run Sanguine Bond (650/1500). On card draw the sources split by trigger: upkeep engines that trade life for cards (Phyrexian Arena 147/484, Black Market Connections 145/484), Vampire-count draw the deck already runs (Champion of Dusk), and death-triggered draw, where the oracle text matters more than the inclusion rate because Edgar's board is mostly tokens and the two cards the death-draw search surfaces first (Midnight Reaper, Grim Haruspex) read 'nontoken'. The August recon's recommendations have landed since: the 99 now runs Command Tower, Anguished Unmaking, Charismatic Conqueror, Elspeth Storm Slayer and Caretaker's Talent.

findings.claim: Malakir Bloodwitch is the most-run drain-carrying Vampire this deck does not have (Lifedrain theme, cards not in the 99: Bloodwitch 261, Twilight Prophet 245, Vampire Nighthawk 154, Vein Ripper 109, Falkenrath Noble 103), and it is the archetype's non-combat finisher. It sits at 261/484 (53.9%) in the Lifedrain theme, 730/1500 (48.7%) in Aristocrats, 1921/3225 (59.6%) in Lifegain and 52% on the commander page overall. A 4/4 flier with protection from white whose ETB drains each opponent for your Vampire count; under eminence that count is high by turn four. Nitpicking Nerds call it 'one of the best Vampires in the deck', say it 'will regularly drain opponents for five or more life' and that it 'can be a finisher in certain games'; Furtado says it 'becomes an instant win card if your board state is big enough to knock everyone out at once'; Wischkaemper calls it 'surprisingly effective as a beater'. With Bloodletter of Aclazotz already in the 99 the ETB drain is doubled on your turn. No two-card line with the 99 in the combo index.

Twilight Prophet is the card the sources name for both halves of the pilot's complaint at once: a repeatable draw that drains. 245/484 (50.6%) Lifedrain, 731/1500 (48.7%) Aristocrats, 1753/3225 (54.4%) Lifegain, 46% overall. A 2/4 flying Vampire for four that, once you control ten permanents, puts the top card into your hand every upkeep and drains each opponent for its mana value while gaining you the same. Gregory lists it under 'card draw and lifegain' as a multi-purpose card; Almeida names it among the cards that 'naturally rewards you for what you're doing' in an Edgar list that prioritises 'CA generated through vampires'. It is a Dark Confidant that gains instead of loses and is a Vampire for eminence. Ascend is the cost: a 36-land deck with eminence tokens reaches ten permanents routinely, but the card does nothing the turn it lands. No two-card line with the 99 in the combo index.

Vein Ripper is the 'big, scary, evasive Vampire with an ability that hurts people' with the strongest card-specific write-ups fetched, and it is not an infinite piece with anything in the 99. A 6/6 flier for six with ward—sacrifice a creature, draining 2 and gaining 2 whenever ANY creature dies (opponents' included, so a symmetric wipe or a chump block drains too). Vrooman ranks it #14 of all death triggers: 'Getting Vein Ripper into play is a death sentence for your opponents'; Price calls it 'like a Blood Artist on steroids for decks that want to sacrifice a lot of creatures or control the board with removal'. Inclusion is second-tier (109/484, 22.5% Lifedrain; 393/1500, 26.2% Aristocrats; 887/3225, 27.5% Lifegain; 19% overall), which the six-mana cost explains. EDHREC's combo page lists exactly one two-card combo (with Tombstone Stairwell, not in the deck); the repo's combo index finds no two-card line with the 99.

The cheap per-death drain tier below Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant is where redundancy lives, and the deck runs none of it. Falkenrath Noble (103/484, 21.3% Lifedrain; 284/1500, 18.9% Aristocrats) is a flying Vampire that drains on ANY creature dying; Vrooman files it with Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance as 'The Mono-Black Aristocrats', his #5 death trigger as a group, and notes Bastion survives 'your sweepers'. Zulaport Cutthroat (Price's #10 most-played mono-black card, '2-drop also drains opponents when creatures die') and Bastion of Remembrance (28/484, 5.8%) hit each opponent rather than one; neither is a Vampire. Vengeful Bloodwitch IS a two-mana Vampire, which Roberts calls 'essentially a functional reprint' of Zulaport on a Vampire body — it triggers eminence where Cutthroat does not. Vindictive Vampire (four-mana Vampire, 1 damage to each opponent and 1 life per death of your creatures) is in Wood's aristocrats list. Nitpicking Nerds' caution applies in reverse here: in the precon Blood Artist and Falkenrath Noble 'won't be reliable finishers' because it lacks sacrifice outlets — this deck has eight. None of these forms a two-card line with the 99.

The gain-to-loss redundancy pieces are SAFE ONLY AFTER Bloodthirsty Conqueror leaves. The combo index finds a bracket-3 two-card infinite between Bloodthirsty Conqueror and each of Marauding Blight-Priest, Epicure of Blood, Cliffhaven Vampire, Defiant Bloodlord and Enduring Tenacity; the deck's own bracket-check reads floor 4 today on exactly this class of line (Conqueror + Vito, Conqueror + Sanguine Bond). With Conqueror out, the 99 holds no loss-to-gain piece, so a gain-to-loss card loops with nothing. Marauding Blight-Priest is the one the sources run: 186/484 (38.4%) Lifedrain, 460/1500 (30.7%) Aristocrats, 985/3225 (30.5%) Lifegain; KrakenTheMeta lists it as the budget card that 'copy[ies] the Sanguine Bond drain effect'; it is a three-mana Vampire. Enduring Tenacity is Dunn's #7 lifegain payoff ('a creature that already has the very relevant I gain life, you lose ability') and returns as an enchantment when it dies; not a Vampire. Defiant Bloodlord (Dunn #34, 'the first instance of slapping a Sanguine Bond on a body') is a seven-mana flying Vampire, redundancy Gregory ran. Cliffhaven Vampire is a four-mana flying Vampire in Orzhov; not listed in any Edgar theme. Each of these, with Vito and Sanguine Bond already in, converts every lifelink hit and every Blood Artist trigger into a second loss — the engine the pilot described, without a loop.

The gain half of the engine, in the sources, is lifelink on evasive Vampire bodies plus one planeswalker, not lifegain spells. Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord is the archetype's planeswalker by a factor of three (226 Lifedrain lists against Sorin, Lord of Innistrad's 78): 226/484 (46.7%) Lifedrain, 712/1500 (47.5%) Aristocrats, 1723/3225 (53.4%) Lifegain — +1 gives a creature deathtouch and lifelink and a counter if it is a Vampire; +1 sacrifices a Vampire for 3 damage and 3 life; -3 cheats a Vampire from hand. Vampire Nighthawk (154/484, 31.8%; 1090/3225, 33.8%) is the flying-deathtouch-lifelink three-drop; Wischkaemper: it 'flying, lifelinks, and deathtouches its way through its life'. Elenda's Hierophant (126/484, 26.0%; 836/3225, 25.9%) is a flying Vampire that grows on every gain and leaves lifelink Vampire tokens equal to its power — Dunn calls it 'probably the best creature with a +1/+1 counter lifegain trigger'. Elenda, Saint of Dusk (Furtado's list) is a lifelink Vampire with hexproof from instants that gets +1/+1 and menace above 40 life and +5/+5 more at 50. Markov Baron is a three-mana lifelink Vampire lord with convoke (Itzlsp's list). Indulging Patrician is a flying lifelink Vampire that drains 3 at end step if you gained 3 (not listed in any Edgar theme). Rhox Faithmender (Dunn #19, 'a Boon Reflection stapled to a 1/5 Rhino') doubles every gain but is not a Vampire and does not attack. None forms a two-card line with the 99.

Death-triggered draw splits on one word, and the inclusion rate does not tell you which side a card is on: Edgar's board is mostly tokens, and the two cards the death-draw search surfaces first read 'nontoken'. Midnight Reaper ('whenever a NONTOKEN creature you control dies') and Grim Haruspex ('whenever another NONTOKEN creature you control dies') are Vrooman's joint #8 death trigger (Gottfried's named card-advantage piece is Morbid Opportunist, not either of them), and Vrooman warns 'the life loss on Midnight Reaper can be an issue'; Harvester of Souls (#7) is nontoken too. The deck already owns that class in High-Society Hunter. The cards that refill from a wipe of eminence tokens are the ones that do NOT say nontoken: Species Specialist (Vrooman #7; name Vampire, draw per Vampire death, tokens included), Dark Prophecy (#8, 'hard to cast' at BBB; every death of yours draws), Liliana's Standard Bearer (flash; draw X for creatures that died under your control this turn — the post-wipe card), Morbid Opportunist (#7, 'don't let the once-per-turn restriction put you off'; Gottfried names it as the card-advantage piece), Vampiric Rites (one-mana enchantment, {1}{B} sac: gain 1 and draw — Gregory's pick, and it feeds Vito), and the instant-speed sacrifice draws cast in response to the wipe: Village Rites (164/484, 33.9% Lifedrain; 581/1500, 38.7% Aristocrats), Corrupted Conviction (same text, 11.9% Aristocrats), Deadly Dispute (67/484; 340/1500, 22.7%) and Plumb the Forbidden (11.7% Aristocrats; copies itself per creature sacrificed, so a wipe becomes draw-N). The deck's token-counting death draw today is two permanents, Liliana, Dreadhorde General and Skullclamp (316/484, 65.3% Lifedrain; Vrooman's #1 death trigger); High-Society Hunter reads nontoken and Bloodtracker draws only for its own counters. It also already holds a sorcery-speed Village Rites on Midgar, City of Mako's adventure, Reactor Raid. Erebos, Bleak-Hearted (pay 2 life per death to draw) is the indestructible version. Vampire Gourmand (Roberts: sacrifice on attack to draw, 'can't be blocked for the turn') and Baron Bertram Graywater ({1}{B}, sac: draw; a lifelink Vampire on every token entry) are the Vampire-bodied options. None forms a two-card line with the 99.

Lifegain-triggered draw exists in exactly two widely-known cards and the sources disagree on whether they are worth a slot. Well of Lost Dreams is Dunn's #9 lifegain payoff ('a one-to-one ratio of mana-to-card-draw is about as good as you can get') and sits in Wood's Edgar aristocrats list; Dawn of Hope is Dunn's #44 ('cheap to play for just 2 mana, and ... it's got its own source of lifelink triggers'). Gregory, writing for Card Kingdom in 2024, shies away from both 'due to the heavy mana sink required to draw cards, and the inflexibility of when that mana is required'. Neither appears in any Edgar theme list. The cheaper Vampire-shaped version is Markov Purifier (three-mana lifelink Vampire; end step, if you gained life, pay {2} to draw) and the Orzhov enchantment Lunar Convocation (Dunn #43; drains 1 at end step if you gained, and {1}{B} pay 2 life: draw). For a deck whose complaint is an empty hand on turn eight with mana open, the mana-sink objection is weaker than it is in Gregory's general case.

The upkeep draw engines drain lists actually run are the life-for-cards ones, which a gain engine pays for. Phyrexian Arena is 147/484 (30.4%) Lifedrain, 380/1500 (25.3%) Aristocrats, 27.8% Lifegain — Price's #6 most-played mono-black card, 'card advantage in exchange for life'. Black Market Connections is 145/484 (30.0%), 455/1500 (30.3%), 26.6% — a card, a Treasure or a 3/2 changeling (a Vampire, so it counts for Bloodwitch and Champion) each turn for life. Necropotence (61/484; 271/1500, 18.1%; Ozymandias' high-power list calls it the primary engine) is a GAME CHANGER, and the deck already holds three (Ancient Tomb, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor), which is the bracket-3 cap — adding it forces bracket 4. Bolas's Citadel is likewise a Game Changer. Vanquisher's Banner (122/484, 25.2%; 308/1500, 20.5%) draws on every Vampire cast and anthems them; Gregory names it beside Twilight Prophet as draw-plus-another-effect. Almeida's Edgar deck tech ranks the generic sorceries (Painful Truths, Read the Bones, Night's Whisper — the last already in) below 'CA generated through vampires'.

The drain archetype's sweeper is one-sided, and it is the most-run sweeper in all three drain-adjacent themes: Olivia's Wrath at 273/484 (56.4%) Lifedrain, 808/1500 (53.9%) Aristocrats, 56.5% Lifegain — ahead of Damn, Ruinous Ultimatum, The Meathook Massacre, Kindred Dominance, Toxic Deluge and Blasphemous Act in each, and in the Aristocrats theme run by more lists than Sanguine Bond (650/1500). Nitpicking Nerds call it an 'overperformer' and 'a one-sided board wipe' that can 'clear the way for all the deck's Vampires'. The deck's mass removal today is Winds of Abandon overloaded and Liliana's -4; nothing else in the 99 touches more than one creature. Behind it: Kindred Dominance (81/484; 248/1500, 16.5%) is the seven-mana version; Damn (129/484, 26.7%; 430/1500, 28.7%) is the flexible one — Almeida: 'Damn can be a targeted removal when needed'; The Meathook Massacre (95/484; 387/1500, 25.8%; Vrooman's #3 death trigger, 'good enough triggers to be cast for X=0') is a sweeper that is ALSO a drain piece, so with it out every Vampire token a wipe kills drains 1; Ruinous Ultimatum (137/484, 28.3%; 316/1500, 21.1%) is the one-sided seven-mana exile; Austere Command and Merciless Eviction are Almeida's 'choose what you want to take away, often saving your field' picks; Toxic Deluge (217/1500, 14.5%) and Blasphemous Act (68/484; 207/1500) are the symmetric cheap ones. With Vein Ripper or Falkenrath Noble out, a symmetric wipe drains for every creature on the table, not just yours.

The big Vampires drain lists run as threats, beyond Bloodwitch, Prophet and Ripper. Patron of the Vein (163/484, 33.7% Lifedrain; 414/1500, 27.6%; 1198/3225, 37.1%) is a six-mana 4/4 flier that kills a creature on entry and grows every Vampire on every opposing death — Nitpicking Nerds' 'go-to finisher'. Butcher of Malakir (115/484, 23.8%; 308/1500, 20.5%) is a seven-mana 5/4 flier that makes each opponent sacrifice whenever your creature dies — Vrooman (#13, with Grave Pact and Dictate of Erebos): 'basically board wipes in a sac deck', 'We've all run our token armies up against the wall of the vampire player with a Butcher of Malakir out'; Wischkaemper: 'both large and destructive'. Drana and Linvala (115/484, 23.8%) is a four-mana 3/5 flying vigilance that shuts off opposing activated abilities and steals them. Vampire Nocturnus (Furtado's and Wood's lists; Wischkaemper: 'one of the most powerful things we can do') gives the whole team +2/+1 and FLYING when the top card is black — but only 38 of this deck's 100 copies carry black (cards.json `colors`; lands are colourless), so the grant is live a little over a third of the time unless the top is controlled. Astarion, the Decadent (Wood's list) is a six-mana deathtouch lifelink Vampire whose Feed mode doubles each opponent's life lost that turn. Sorin Markov (46/484) sets an opponent to 10. Archfiend of Despair (Itzlsp's list) is the eight-mana doubler of all life lost. Olivia, Crimson Bride (260/1500, 17.3%; 756/3225, 23.4%) reanimates on attack and is a graveyard card; recorded, not endorsed.

Two drain finishers the sources run are flagged because they are kill lines with the 99 rather than infinites. Blood Tribute (111/484, 22.9% Lifedrain; 841/3225, 26.1% Lifegain) halves a target opponent's life and, kicked by tapping a Vampire, gains you that much; the combo index records Blood Tribute + Vito and Blood Tribute + Bloodletter of Aclazotz as bracket-4 'target opponent loses the game' lines (halve, then Vito drains the same again, or Bloodletter doubles the loss). Not a loop, and not a two-card infinite, but it is a six-mana one-player kill with two cards already in the 99. Exsanguinate (92/484, 19.0%; 193/1500, 12.9%; 17.9% Lifegain) is the X-drain that Itzlsp files as the deck's 'Finisher'; with Vito it drains X per opponent and then 3X more to one target, with Bloodletter it is 2X on your turn — large, not infinite. Neither forms a two-card infinite in the combo index.

Outlets are not the gap, and the sources' preference is for free ones with a visible payoff. The deck already runs eight (Viscera Seer, Yahenni, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Vish Kal, Ashnod's Altar, Altar of Dementia). Gottfried: 'I'll be focusing on the free ones', naming Warren Soultrader as 'essentially free in our 40-life format' and Priest of Forgotten Gods (also in Ozymandias' list) — both draw or make mana on the sacrifice rather than only enabling it. Roberts' Ruthless Lawbringer ('spot removal with fangs') is the Vampire-bodied outlet that destroys a nonland permanent on entry. Carrying the pilot's direction toward big Vampires, these are recorded for completeness; an outlet that also draws (Vampiric Rites, Baron Bertram Graywater, Vampire Gourmand — see the draw finding) does more for the stated complaint than a ninth bare outlet.

Edgar Markov has no cEDH presence: the cEDH Decklist Database contains no deck with 'Edgar' anywhere on the page (confirmed 2026-09-30); the only Mardu entries are Celes, Rune Knight and the Dargo + Tymna pairing. EDHREC's commander page counts 51,322 Edgar decks, tagged Vampires 5.9K, Lifegain 3.2K, Tokens 2.1K, Aggro 1.5K; the Lifedrain tag is a 484-deck subset. Collins (Commander's Herald) records the social reading: Edgar 'routinely elicits groans when a player reveals him in the command zone', eminence 'would be the go-to example of why the mechanic was bad', and he is banned in Duel Commander. For the bracket frame: the deck's own bracket-check reads floor 4 today on two two-card infinites both through Bloodthirsty Conqueror, and three Game Changers (Ancient Tomb, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor), which is the bracket-3 cap. Cutting Conqueror alone brings the floor to 3; adding any Game Changer (Necropotence, Bolas's Citadel) or any loss-to-gain card (Exquisite Blood) sends it back to 4.

known_failure_modes: Emptying the hand into a sweeper. Almeida (Cardsrealm Edgar deck tech): 'it is very common for aggressive decks to play all cards in their hand and be unable to recover after a sweeper.' This is the pilot's turn-7-8 complaint stated from the other side: eminence pays you to cast every Vampire, and the draw that exists (Champion of Dusk, Welcoming Vampire, Skullclamp) is front-loaded on casting and entering, not on dying.

Drain without death. Nitpicking Nerds on the precon: Blood Artist and Falkenrath Noble 'won't be reliable finishers like they normally are' because the deck lacks sacrifice outlets and so only drains when someone wipes. This deck has the outlets, but the Forge seat does not use them (the record on Viscera Seer and Ashnod's Altar is in docs/gotchas-bench.md), so a Forge rate on this deck's drain is a floor; a trigger (Bloodwitch ETB, Prophet upkeep, Ripper on any death) is measurable where an activation is not.

Solitaire turns. Gottfried (EDHREC aristocrats guide): 'Aristocrats decks have a reputation for taking long, solitaire-esque turns with very little having changed at the end of them', and the cure he names is payoffs that make each sacrifice matter — the reason the drain tier is the thing to deepen rather than the outlet tier.

Self-inflicted life loss on the draw engines. Vrooman on Midnight Reaper: 'the life loss on Midnight Reaper can be an issue'; Phyrexian Arena, Dark Prophecy, Black Market Connections and Champion of Dusk all cost life. In a gain engine that is a feature until the gain pieces are removed, after which the deck is paying life into an empty board.

Being the archenemy from turn two. Collins: Edgar 'routinely elicits groans when a player reveals him in the command zone'. Every primer fetched in August treated an unanswered Edgar board as lethal within a turn cycle, so the table finds the wipe; the August recon's 'lords eat removal' read (Gregory) still holds.
contested: Whether lifegain-triggered draw is worth a slot. Dunn (2026) ranks Well of Lost Dreams #9 of all lifegain payoffs; Gregory (2024) 'shy[s] away from Well of Lost Dreams and Dawn of Hope these days due to the heavy mana sink required'. Neither appears in any Edgar theme list. The objection is about mana flexibility, and this deck's complaint is specifically mana with nothing to spend it on.

Nontoken death draw in a token deck. Midnight Reaper and Grim Haruspex are the cards every aristocrats source names; both read 'nontoken' and so miss every eminence token. Species Specialist, Dark Prophecy, Liliana's Standard Bearer and Vampiric Rites do not. No source makes this distinction for Edgar; it is read from oracle text.

More gain-to-loss copies versus more gain sources. Marauding Blight-Priest, Enduring Tenacity, Defiant Bloodlord and Cliffhaven Vampire all stack with Vito and Sanguine Bond (each gain event drains once per copy), but every one of them is a two-card infinite with Bloodthirsty Conqueror while it remains in the 99. The sources run Blight-Priest (30-38%) and not the others; whether a third or fourth Sanguine Bond is better than a Vampire Nighthawk is not settled anywhere fetched.

Olivia, Crimson Bride and the graveyard. 17-23% of drain lists run her; she is a reanimation card and the pilot's August direction excluded the graveyard. The 2026-09-29 direction is silent on it. Recorded in the threat finding, not endorsed.

Whether Skullclamp is 'draw on death'. It is — the equipped 1/1 token dies and draws two — and it is Vrooman's #1 death trigger and 65.3% of Lifedrain lists; the deck already runs it. The August recon filed it as contested because it is a sacrifice engine in disguise; under the new direction that objection no longer applies.

gaps: Moxfield: blocked, confirmed 2026-09-30 — the search surfaced a 'High Powered Vampires (No game changers Needed)' primer at moxfield.com/decks/fJLkugdUHE2lyvZPjcwpaA/primer that would be the closest thing to a bracket-3 drain Edgar primer; it could not be fetched and nothing from it is recorded.

TappedOut returned HTTP 403 on two different deck URLs on 2026-09-30 (it was fetchable for the August recon), so the 'Edgar Markov's Vampire Horde [Primer]', 'Edgar Markov Aristocrats EDH' and the 'Is Twilight Prophet worthwhile?' forum thread are not cited.
tcgplaymatpros.com returned HTTP 402; TCGplayer's Edgar guide returned an empty body (as in August); ajaxalternates.com redirected to its shop homepage. None is cited.

No fetchable primer exists for a drain-engine Edgar WITHOUT the Exquisite Blood loop. Every drain list fetched (Itzlsp, Gregory, Furtado, Ozymandias) runs Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror beside Sanguine Bond or Vito. The pilot's bracket-3 constraint is more purist than any published drain list, so the gain-to-loss findings here are 'what the loop-running lists run, minus the loop'.

EDHREC theme card lists truncate at roughly fifty cards per type, so 'not listed' for Zulaport Cutthroat, Midnight Reaper, Grim Haruspex, Species Specialist, Liliana's Standard Bearer, Dawn of Hope, Well of Lost Dreams, Cliffhaven Vampire and Epicure of Blood means below the cut, not zero. No per-commander inclusion rate for any of them is recorded.

No source measures the pilot's specific complaint — 0-2 cards in hand after turn 7-8. Almeida and Nitpicking Nerds assert the run-out-of-steam failure qualitatively; the goldfish's draw channel on this list is the instrument that would quantify it, and a model_draw figure before and after a death-draw swap is what would settle which trigger class (token-counting versus nontoken) actually refills.

The Draftsim aristocrats and lifegain rankings are format-wide, not Edgar-specific; Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance, Liliana's Standard Bearer and Species Specialist have no card-specific Edgar write-up anywhere fetched, only a rank in a general list.
The 'guide at the bottom' of Ozymandias' Archidekt list did not render through the fetch; only its card list is recorded.
